candidates.name: Michael Dublin
candidates.summary: Educator and activist running on an ecosocialist platform.

biography.text: Dublin describes himself as an educator and activist.

positions.text: Supports a $25 federal minimum wage and higher taxes on wealthy people.
Supports a Green New Deal, public ownership of major polluters and a transition to renewable energy.

candidates.name: Roy Cooper
candidates.summary: Former two-term governor and former state attorney general.

biography.text: Cooper served two terms as governor after serving as North Carolina attorney general and in the General Assembly.

positions.text: Supports restoring enhanced ACA tax credits, reversing Medicaid cuts, expanding Medicare drug negotiation and limiting surprise billing.
Campaigns on lowering household costs, including food, health care, housing, utilities and child care.

record.text: As governor, Cooper supported the bipartisan 2023 law that expanded Medicaid in North Carolina.

candidates.name: Shannon W. Bray
candidates.summary: Technology professional and Navy veteran emphasizing limited government and civil liberties.

biography.text: Bray's campaign describes him as a technology professional and Navy veteran.

positions.text: Supports simplifying the tax code, ending corporate subsidies and capping federal spending.
Emphasizes constitutional limits, decentralization and individual rights.

candidates.name: Michael Whatley
candidates.summary: Attorney and former chair of the Republican National Committee and North Carolina Republican Party.

biography.text: Whatley led the Republican National Committee during the 2024 election cycle and previously chaired the state Republican Party.

positions.text: Supports stronger border enforcement and large-scale deportations.
Supports lower federal spending and expanded production of reliable, affordable energy.
States support for gun rights, restrictions on abortion and removing what he calls woke ideology from schools.

candidates.name: Maad Abu-Ghazalah
candidates.summary: Entrepreneur and animal-rescue advocate.

biography.text: The official ballot lists Abu-Ghazalah as the Libertarian nominee in District 7.

positions.text: No detailed campaign platform was found in the sources reviewed.

candidates.name: Kimberly Hardy
candidates.summary: Social-work professor and small-business owner.

biography.text: Hardy is a social-work professor whose campaign focuses on families, education and regional opportunity.

positions.text: Supports raising the federal minimum wage, overtime protections, tax relief on tips and more small-business lending.
Supports clean-water protections, stormwater and flood-resilience infrastructure, clean energy and continued FEMA funding.
Supports protecting Medicare and Medicaid and lowering insurance and prescription-drug costs.

referenda.title: Photo identification amendment
referenda.summary: Would require all voters, including absentee voters, to present photo identification before voting.

referenda.title: Income-tax cap amendment
referenda.summary: Would prevent the state income-tax rate from being raised above 3.5 percent.

referenda.title: Property-tax limits amendment
referenda.summary: Would require limits on property-tax increases by local governments.

referenda.title: New Hanover County school bonds
referenda.summary: Would authorize $320.525 million in school-facility bonds. The ballot estimates $500.378 million in principal and interest and a $5 annual property-tax increase per $100,000 of value, including anticipated endowment grants.
